summary: Discovery call focusing on embedding-based reranking use case. Stratacore currently runs keyword-first search with Elastic and wants to add embeddings for semantic reranking while keeping BM25 for recall. Key concerns: latency at 200-500 QPS, vector DB choice/integration, dimensionality (512 vs 768), cold-start ingestion time for 1M+ vectors, and security requirements for PII. Discussed Redwood hosting options (hosted API for quick POC, dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, private/VPC for data residency). Agreed on running a throughput benchmark and scheduling a hybrid-search technical deep dive.
topics: Vector DB integration options (managed vs self-hosted)

transcript:
Meeting: Embeddings & Reranking Discovery - Stratacore
Date/Time: 2027-09-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Jesse Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Stratacore Head of Search), Marcus Li (ML Infra), Aisha Khan (PM)

[00:00] Jesse: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intro, i'm jesse on the ae side, priya is our se who will go deep on performance, how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena: good, thanks, excited to walk through our current stack, i'll be leading the product side, marcus on infra and aisha here for prioritization.
[00:22] Priya: great, i'll start with a quick overview of how teams typically wire embeddings + rerank into their search stack and then we can go into your constraints. sound good?
[00:30] Marcus: yep good.
[00:33] Priya: ok so typical pattern is index with your vector DB (pinecone/weaviate/milvus/elastic), at query time you do a nearest-neighbor search to get top-K then optionally run a neural reranker or a cross-encoder to reorder the top results. Redwood can host embeddings and reranking or you can run dedicated pools.
[00:50] Lena: right — we currently use elastic for inverted index and BM25 for recall. we want to add semantic signals for better recall on hard queries. main ask is minimal latency impact and predictable cost.
[01:05] Jesse: got it. what's your current qps and latency targets?
[01:08] Lena: baseline is about 300 qps peak, average 120 qps. for rerank we want p95 below 150ms, p99 ideally under 300ms.
[01:20] Priya: okay that helps. for 300 qps at 150ms p95 we're generally looking at Dedicated or high-tier hosted with batching turned down — dedicated gives you guaranteed GPUs which simplifies meeting p99s.
[01:35] Marcus: curious about throughput numbers — like how many vectors per second can your dedicated pool ingest and what about bulk import for 1M vectors?
[01:45] Priya: ingestion depends on embedding model and batch size; for a typical 768-d model and RTX A100-class infra, we can do ~2k embeddings/sec with optimized pipelines, more with async bulk loaders. for CPU-hosted embeddings it's slower. for import of 1M vectors you should budget a few hours with streaming ingestion; we usually recommend an initial bulk job and then ongoing incremental streaming.
[02:10] Marcus: a few hours is ok, but network egress and spot interruptions matter for us — we'll need private deployment or VPC peering.
[02:20] Jesse: on that note, our Private offering supports VPC peering and on-prem options, plus KMS integration for keys. is SOC 2 a hard requirement?
[02:30] Aisha: yes, any vendor needs SOC 2 Type II, and ability to attest to data residency for EU customers. also RBAC and audit logs.
[02:40] Jesse: we can share SOC2 docs and an architecture diagram for VPC setup.
[02:45] Lena: good. another question: dimensionality — we have 512-d legacy embeddings but evaluating 768-d from newer encoders; it's a cost/latency tradeoff. how much does 768 vs 512 change throughput?
[02:58] Priya: roughly linear with vector size — 768 increases memory and compute by ~1.5x compared to 512. search latency and storage both increase; however quality sometimes improves, so it's a trade. also quantization can help (8-bit or 4-bit) for storage and memory while preserving recall for many models.
[03:15] Marcus: do you support automatic on-the-fly quantization or do we need to quantize before ingestion?
[03:22] Priya: we support serving quantized models in Dedicated and Private. for vector DBs, some support compressed storage, others require pre-quantized vectors. we usually recommend testing both options in the benchmark.
[03:35] Lena: hybrid search — we want to keep BM25 for recall and then blend semantic score with BM25. what's the recommended architecture?
[03:45] Priya: common approach: compute BM25 top N (e.g., 100) from Elastic, then run vector nearest neighbor on that candidate set or retrieve vector top-K and then merge scores. Another is late fusion where you retrieve top candidates from both and then rerank with a cross-encoder.
[04:05] Marcus: merging results increases complexity — any examples of throughput impact?
[04:10] Priya: yes late fusion is heavier because you run multiple retrieval ops; reranking only the top 10-50 is lighter. if you can keep vector NN limited to the candidate set from BM25 you'll reduce vector DB QPS significantly.
[04:25] Aisha: what about cost modeling — tokens vs embedding ops vs vector DB?
[04:30] Jesse: pricing for Redwood hosted embedding calls is per-embedding unit; reranking/computed neural score also billed as inference. Dedicated is contract-based with predictable cost per GPU-hour. we can send a cost model spreadsheet.
[04:45] Lena: can we run a POC where we push 1M vectors and simulate 300 qps to measure end-to-end latency including Elastic?
[04:55] Priya: absolutely — we usually do two-phase benchmarks: ingest + cold queries to measure index time and then steady-state qps with warm cache. we'll provide an ingestion script and sample harness.
[05:10] Marcus: network architecture — will we need to open ports for vector db or will you provide a connector?
[05:16] Priya: for hosted, we expose endpoint over TLS; for VPC/private we can do peering or a connector with a customer-managed gateway. we'll share a networking checklist.
[05:28] Lena: anything about reranker model choice — cross-encoder vs bi-encoder? which gives best relevance for short queries?
[05:36] Priya: cross-encoders are more accurate but computationally expensive; typical pattern is bi-encoder for recall and a small cross-encoder for rerank on top-K. Redwood supports running both and can fall back to cheaper models when capacity is constrained.
[05:52] Marcus: do you support model pinning and rollouts? we need tested model versions for production.
[05:56] Jesse: yes, dedicated and private allow version pinning, canaries and A/B rollouts via console.
[06:05] Aisha: any pitfalls you commonly see when teams adopt embeddings + rerank?
[06:10] Priya: a few: not normalizing scores between BM25 and vector scores, not accounting for cold cache, and underestimating downstream cross-encoder cost. also data leakage for PII if you send raw text to hosted endpoints without proper controls.
[06:25] Lena: we have PII scrubbing upstream but need to confirm KMS options.
[06:30] Jesse: we'll include KMS/HSM integration details in the security pack.
[06:35] Priya: for performance numbers, do you have sample query length and distribution? short queries vs multi-sentence?
[06:42] Lena: mostly short queries 1-3 tokens, some long multi-sentence queries from research use-cases.
[06:48] Priya: short queries favor lexical recall, so hybrid approach often gives best of both worlds. also consider using a slightly larger vector dim for catch-all queries, but test quality delta during POC.
[07:05] Marcus: for the POC, what infra would you recommend — hosted with burst vs a small dedicated cluster?
[07:12] Priya: if you need to hit p99 targets deterministically at 300 qps, i'd recommend a small dedicated cluster to start. hosted is faster to spin up and cheaper for exploratory work.
[07:25] Lena: timeline — we'd like a POC within 3 weeks and decision in 8 weeks.
[07:30] Jesse: that's reasonable. we'll come back with pricing and benchmark plan this week.
[07:35] Aisha: question on dimensionality again — if we go with 512 embeddings to save cost, will recall suffer for entity-based queries?
[07:44] Priya: sometimes entity recall drops a bit; it's very dataset dependent. our eval harness can run per-query-type A/B tests to measure degradation.
[07:55] Marcus: for vector DB choice — we prefer not to manage another datastore if possible. is Redwood able to host vector storage within Dedicated?
[08:03] Jesse: Dedicated can include managed vector store as an add-on; Private supports your own vector DB behind the VPC. we'll outline tradeoffs in the doc.
[08:12] Lena: how do you handle schema changes or vector re-indexing?
[08:16] Priya: we support rolling re-index jobs, sharded imports, and can do online reindex with blue/green style transitions to avoid downtime.
[08:27] Aisha: security again — SSO and RBAC details?
[08:31] Jesse: we support SAML/SCIM for SSO and RBAC roles in Console; audit logs are part of enterprise plan.
[08:40] Marcus: do you have any benchmarks showing 300 qps with p99 < 300ms for rerank?
[08:46] Priya: we have internal profiles and public benchmarks; we'll include sample numbers but recommend running a tailored benchmark since results vary by query shape and model.
[09:00] Lena: ok next, what's the integration effort for our product team? we have an Elastic pipeline and will need a small orchestration layer to call embeddings/rerank endpoints.
[09:10] Priya: typically 2-4 sprints for a minimal integration (ingestion, query-time calls, metrics). with our SDKs and example connectors to Elastic it's faster.
[09:22] Jesse: shall we summarize next steps?
[09:25] Lena: yes please.
[09:26] Jesse: action items: priya will send benchmark plan and ingestion scripts; i'll send pricing and security docs; lena will share data volumes and example query logs; we schedule a deep technical session wk of 9/27. anything else?
[09:40] Aisha: could you also include a cost model example?
[09:43] Jesse: yes, i'll attach a cost spreadsheet.
[09:45] Lena: thanks all, this was helpful.
[09:47] Jesse: awesome, thanks everyone — we'll follow up by end of week.
[09:50] (call ends)
